newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, no end to sluggish trend.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, no end to sluggish trend.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Wednesday with losses to some blue chips, and market participants saw no end to the sluggish trend before nationwide local elections on April 13.
"Although local elections may not be of supreme importance, what is expected now is some sign of political stabilisation," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage.
"Until then I don't expect any move forward," he said.
However, traders predicted growth for Zagrebacka Banka amid expectations it would soon release good profit figures for 1996.
Zagrebacka's ordinary stock was among three losers on Wednesday, edging down 44 kuna to 1,806 on volume of 55 shares.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva was flat at 450 kuna on volume of 446 shares. Its Zagreb price overshot London, where it traded in a $14.5-14.75 range.
"Unless Pliva's price rises in London, we can expect it to fall mildly in Zagreb as well," Nikolac said.
Three out a total of 12 active issues rose and six were flat. Volume was slightly higher at 6,858 shares, turnover rose to 2.4 million kuna from 1.9 million kuna.
Top loser was cable maker Elka, falling 34 kuna to 111 with 200 shares traded in two transactions. It was followed by hotelier Suncani Hvar, down six kuna to 60 on volume of 1,184.
Most active food stock Podravka also led gainers, inching up one kuna to 291 on volume of 3,714 shares.
Hotelier Laguna rose 10 kuna to 1,450, with 329 shares changing hands. Electric manufacturer Koncar inched up five kuna to 1,155, with 34 units traded.
Nikolac said Podravka may escape the fate of stocks such as chocolate maker Kras and Elka, included in mass privatisation, for which he foresaw very slow trade in the near future.
"For Podravka on the contrary, there is an obvious long-term interest of foreign investors," he added.
Kras joined ranks with stocks that held their ground, including hotelier Jadranturist, Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf and brewery Karlovacka pivovara.
Some companies -- like Jadranturist, Laguna and Janaf -- whose assets were not earmarked to be exchanged for free vouchers, were seen as among the most attractive shares in the weeks ahead.
